page: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an ARM-based virtual instance powered by first-generation AWS Graviton processors built on the ARM Cortex-A72 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the system provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a fixed frequency of 2.3 GHz without hyperthreading. Cache specifications detail a 32 KB L1 data cache per core and a shared 2 MB L2 cache, with no L3 cache present. The platform includes 16.0 GB of RAM allocated at 2.0 GB per core, hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support, zero local storage, and 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear execution profiles across workloads. Multi-core synthetic compute testing via stress-ng shows average performance with a score of 11,904.08, whereas single-core performance remains limited, recorded at 410.0 in Geekbench single-core and 3,170.47 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth results fall into lower percentile tiers, reporting 23.51 GB/sec for uncached 256MB read operations and 8.88 GB/sec for uncached write operations. Additional application tests indicate 2.41 GB/sec throughput for static web serving and 4.24 million operations per second in Redis SET performance.

The a1.2xlarge instance presents a budget-oriented hardware profile suited for ARM-native application deployments. The architectural absence of L3 cache and advanced x86 vector extensions limits per-core execution speeds in compute-heavy or floating-point tasks, representing a key technical tradeoff. However, the 8-core allocation combined with 16 GB RAM offers functional resource density for lightweight microservices, arm64 software compilation, basic web servers, and distributed caching instances.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an ARM-based instance driven by 8 dedicated physical cores of first-generation AWS Graviton silicon running at 2.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core), 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, hardware AES encryption, and no local disk storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates average multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng (11,904.08), but exhibits lower scores in single-core tasks, uncached memory bandwidth (23.51 GB/sec read, 8.88 GB/sec write), and static web serving (2.41 GB/sec). With its lower single-threaded throughput and lack of L3 cache or AVX instructions, the instance offers a budget-conscious tradeoff for arm64-compatible architectures. It is suitable for lightweight microservices, basic web serving, development nodes, and distributed caching workloads where core count and energy-efficient scale-out take precedence over maximum single-core compute speeds.
